description: The factory has exactly two phases. BUILD alternates one author and one auditor per lane until the release-train criteria hold. GATE is release-engineer-exclusive: no builder, auditor, compliance, or crouton-alpha dispatch runs while the release-engineer owns the section. The release-engineer may spawn exactly one hacker campaign for the whole train; that is the only hacker edge in GATE. A refused release returns to BUILD for the bounded repair; a merged release returns to BUILD for the next section. This file is the only definition of the phase rules; personas, SOPs, and schemas cite it and do not restate the values.
k1_rule: One K1 run per lane, at most k1_total host-wide, no queue. A lane whose K1 slot is busy is not dispatched; the caller retries after factory k1 down or TTL expiry. A second K1 on one lane is refused with K1_SLOT_BUSY.

BUILD.purpose: Author, then audit, one lane at a time; never both on the same lane.
BUILD.lane_rule: A builder, compliance, crouton-alpha, or auditor dispatch names exactly one permanent lane. Compliance may run lane-less only for a spec-wide read, and then it dispatches no writer.
BUILD.exclusivity_rule: At most one active author and one active auditor per lane, never both. The latest dispatch record for a lane is the active owner: an auditor target is active until a later RECORD/HALT/DISPATCH for that lane; an author target is active until a later RECORD/HALT/DISPATCH for that lane. A dispatch that would put an author and an auditor on the same lane at the same time is refused with PHASE_LANE_BUSY.
BUILD.alternation_rule: Within one task on one lane, the order is author -> auditor. A second author dispatch is legal only after the auditor returned BLOCK (repair) or after the task's verdict is recorded. A second auditor dispatch on the same (head, tree) is legal only for a permitted fault re-audit or the delta audit of a repair.
release_train_criteria: the release_train trigger in this file: 6 completed tasks or 6 hours since the section opened, whichever first
every active permanent lane has a recorded auditor verdict PASS at the section head/tree
no lane has an active author or auditor dispatch
no HALT/PARKED record is open for the lineage
the live policy_digest and control_set_sha match the newest gate-control proof
the integration worktree is clean at the reconciled section head

GATE.purpose: Release the audited section; the release-engineer is the only active role, with exactly one hacker campaign as its child.
GATE.hacker_campaign_rule: The active release-engineer may spawn exactly one hacker campaign covering the whole release train. No orchestrator->hacker dispatch exists, and no second hacker campaign may be recorded during the gate.
GATE.lane_rule: The release-engineer dispatch is lane-less (spec-comp is the integration target and is resolved by worktree-map.json). No lane worktree is dispatched or written.
GATE.exclusivity_rule: Exactly one release-engineer invocation is active. Its only child is the single train campaign (hacker). No author, auditor, compliance, or crouton-alpha dispatch, and no second hacker dispatch, may be recorded until the release result is recorded.
GATE.exit_rule: A proof-recorded release record with phase MERGED ends the gate and returns the factory to BUILD for the next section. A proof-recorded release record with result_type REFUSED, or an orchestrator CYCLES_EXHAUSTED/RELEASE_REFUSED decision, returns to BUILD for the bounded repair loop.

requires: every active lane has a recorded verdict PASS
no active author or auditor dispatch on any lane
transitions.record: orchestrator dispatch record with phase=GATE, action=DISPATCH, target=release-engineer, and evidence_refs naming every lane PASS verdict

requires: a proof-recorded release result (MERGED, or REFUSED with a CI_*/CHECKS_*/MERGE_REJECTED/STATE_MISMATCH reason), or an orchestrator CYCLES_EXHAUSTED/RELEASE_REFUSED record
transitions.record: orchestrator dispatch record with phase=BUILD, action=RECORD, target=none, and the recorded release ref

requires: the release-engineer returned a refusal that permits a repaired head
the orchestrator records the repair was routed to BUILD first; this self-edge exists only for the record of the refusal, never for a second merge on the same head
transitions.record: orchestrator dispatch record with phase=GATE, action=RECORD, target=none, refusal reason

invariants: No phase is inferred from prose, a prompt, or a result body; it is read from the latest recorded dispatch record for the lineage.
A phase record is append-only. A transition writes one new record; it never edits the prior phase record.
A HALT ends the turn and freezes the phase until a human-authored capability resumes it.
The orchestrator holds routing authority only; the phase does not grant it code, verdict, or merge authority.

The release-engineer's only child is one hacker campaign per release train at GATE; it may not dispatch any other role. The auditor's only child is one hacker campaign in BUG_FINDING. The orchestrator never dispatches the hacker, and no other parent/child edge exists.

conditions: 6 completed tasks in the section, whichever first
6 hours since the section opened, whichever first
every active permanent lane has a recorded auditor verdict PASS at the section head/tree
no lane has an active author or auditor dispatch
no HALT/PARKED record is open for the lineage
the live policy_digest and control_set_sha match the newest gate-control proof
the integration worktree is clean at the reconciled section head
release_train.task_count_source: recorded dispatch records for the lineage that reach a PASS verdict at the section head; a re-audit or repair does not count as a new task
release_train.clock_source: proof store timestamps from the first BUILD dispatch of the section to now; never the model session clock
release_train.on_trigger: the orchestrator records phase=GATE and dispatches one release-engineer; it does not wait for a seventh task or the next hour
release_train.on_refusal: a REFUSED release returns to BUILD for the bounded repair; the section clock continues and the cycle cap still applies

capability_lifecycle.rule: A completed bound tool call slides the idle window to now + idle_ttl_seconds. An idle-expired but otherwise valid capability is reminted transparently with remint_reason IDLE_EXPIRY; the old id is superseded, never reused. Re-mint at 6 hours or 6 tasks, whichever first, with parent_task_id, fresh head/tree, and the remaining allowance. The handler is factory CLI.
